did_you_know.text: Did you know? In the first vision in Zechariah 5, he sees a flying scroll—not a scroll lying still, but one moving through the sky before his eyes.
Did you know? The scroll is described as twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide, so its dimensions are given precisely as part of the vision.
Did you know? The angel calls the scroll “the curse”—a curse or an oath of punishment—and it goes out over the whole land against the thief and against the one who swears falsely.

Did you know? According to the vision, the curse does not merely affect the person himself: it enters the house of the thief or of the one who swears falsely, remains there, and destroys it, along with its timbers and stones.
Did you know? After the vision of the scroll, the angel speaking with Zechariah directs his attention to another vision and asks him what he sees coming out.

Did you know? In the second vision, an ephah—a measuring vessel—appears, and it is said, “This is their appearance throughout the whole land.” Thus, the text connects the vision with reality throughout the land.
Did you know? A woman sits inside the ephah, and when the angel explains the vision, he says, “This is wickedness.” He then throws a lead disk over her and shuts her inside the ephah.
Did you know? Two winged women carry the ephah between the earth and the sky. Their wings are described as the wings of a stork.
Did you know? The ephah’s destination is the land of Shinar. There a house will be built for it, and it will be placed on its base—a fixed foundation or appointed place.
